summary: Carroll County site the FFLA lists as a Map Table, not a tower; another list says it once had a fire tower; no source found describes it today.

facts.status_note: Forest Lookouts marks the entry Removed; the FFLA lists it as gone, type Map Table

events.note: Forest Lookouts quotes a 1921-22 Forestry Commission report on improved service to the mountain; not a build or closing date

evidence.supports: FFLA lists Mount Chocorua in Carroll County as a Map Table site, gone
evidence.quote: Chocorua, Mount Carroll 43.95427 -71.27320 Map Table Gone

evidence.supports: NH Family Hikes lists Mount Chocorua among mountains that once had a fire tower
evidence.quote: Mountains which Once Had a Fire Tower

evidence.supports: NH Family Hikes places Mount Chocorua in Albany at 3,500 feet
1922 note on improved service to the mountain by changing the line from the Liberty trail to the Bee Line trail
evidence.quote: The service to Mount Chocorua was improved by changing the line from Liberty trail to the Bee Line trail.

evidence.supports: the 1922 note is credited to the Forestry Commission biennial report of 1921-22
the Forest Lookouts page lists the entry as Removed
the Forest Lookouts page gives only the county as a description of the site

corrections.why: The FFLA lists the Chocorua site as Map Table. The only tower claim found is the NH Family Hikes list of mountains that once had a fire tower, so the type is disputed and should be flagged.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLA lists a Map Table; NH Family Hikes says the mountain once had a fire tower. No dated source for a tower was found, so the story reports both listings and does not pick one.

notes_for_editor: Thin evidence: no build date, builder, staffing, fire or present-day description for this site. The NHDFL history PDF (nhdfl.dncr.nh.gov, forest-lookout-towers-history.pdf) returned HTTP 403 to fetch_text. A search snippet from it lists an NHTOA station at Chocorua; that is unverified and not quoted, so please check the PDF by hand. The Chocorua Lake Conservancy history lists summit fires in 1882, 1903 and 1915, but none is tied to a lookout, so they are left out of the story. Brief record says kind tower; see corrections.
